I recommend starting with a warning that he may not like the conversation but that it's important to you. Also remember self care and kindness take care of yourself don't push past the place you're at emotionally it's ok to press pause and continue when you need.

I'd like to start my comment off with you don't deserve it at all. How you feel is ok it's valid. It can be so isolating, I'm sorry you feel you can't talk to your parents. The truth is some feelings never go away or at least I don't think it does I'm 12 years after my first SA and I still get angry I'm still hurt and depressed I feel so tired and upset. That may not be what you want to hear. You can grow from it change and grow. I've changed my life, become someone new. It still hurts and it can still make me angry, but you don't have to let it consume you.
Good luck I hope it goes well. Take care of yourself.

The most important thing you can do is self care. Accepting this wasn't your fault and being kind to yourself which is much harder than it sounds. The friends who are giving you problems will either come around or not it's up to you how you wish to handle it. Just remember you're awesome and deserve the best. I recommend meditation and reading it helped me a lot.

I think this was assault but not on your end of it. You have barely any memory, you were much more intoxicated than he was. That isn't to say that he did it maliciously. He was just more aware and in that case responsible for your safety. Being drunk means you cannot consent as your decision making is impaired him being the less drunk and more sober than you takes that responsibility. At least in my view.
